name.text: Counting Words with Specific Letter Constraints

questiontext.text:
1. Conside the word {@word1@}.

Assuming that any arrangement of the letters in {@word1@} forms a word, how many different words can we make with the letters of {@word1@}?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

2. Consider the word {@word2@}.

Assuming that any arrangement of the letters in {@word2@} forms a word, how many different words can we make with the letters of {@word2@}?

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

3. Consider the word {@word3@}.

Assuming that any arrangement of the letters in {@word3@} forms a word, how many different words can we make with the letters of {@word3@}?

[[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

\(1.\)

The word {@word1@} has {@wordlength1@} letters, all of which are different. Therefore, the number of words we can make is the number of possible arrangements (or permutations) of the letters of the word {@word1@}. This is given by \({@wordlength1@}! = {@wordlength1!@}\).


\(2.\)

The word {@word2@} has {@wordlength2@} letters. Therefore, the number of words we can make is the number of possible arrangements (or permutations) of the letters of the word {@word2@}. This is given by \({@wordlength2@}! = {@wordlength2!@}\).

However, the letter {@letter2@} appears twice in the word {@word2@} and many options in the number above will be repeated. As {@letter2@} appears twice, we consider the number of ways in which these two letters could be arranged. We have 2 options for the first one and 1 option for the second one. So there are \(2\cdot 1 = 2! = 2\) ways to arrange the two letters {@letter2@}.

Therefore, the number of words, without repetition, is given by \(\displaystyle \frac{{@wordlength2@}!}{2!} = \frac{{@wordlength2!@}}{2} = {@ta2@}\).


\(3.\)

The word {@word3@} has {@wordlength3@} letters. Therefore, the number of words we can make is the number of possible arrangements (or permutations) of the letters of the word {@word3@}. This is given by \({@wordlength3@}! = {@wordlength3!@}\).

However, the letter {@letter3@} appears three times in the word {@word3@} and many options in the number above will be repeated. As {@letter3@} appears three times, we consider the number of ways in which these three letters could be arranged. We have 3 options for the first one, 2 options for the second one and 1 option for the third one. So there are \(3\cdot 2\cdot 1 = 3! = 6\) ways to arrange the three letters {@letter3@}.

Therefore, the number of words, without repetition, is given by \(\displaystyle \frac{{@wordlength3@}!}{3!} = \frac{{@wordlength3!@}}{6} = {@ta3@}\).
